label: TP
reason: User input directly flows into the LDAP filter string via concatenation without any sanitization or escaping, reaching two sinks: (1) the filter used in ctx.search(), enabling LDAP injection, and (2) echoed to the HTTP response via encodeForHTML() which still reflects unescaped portions of the original input in contexts outside HTML entities. The ESAPI encoder protects against XSS in rendered strings but does not sanitize special characters needed for LDAP syntax, leaving the underlying injection risk intact.

evidence.note: param injected into LDAP filter and echoed to response without proper neutralization
